land.text: Tetzcoco and the Acolhua kingdoms of the eastern Basin

successors.note: 'founded in 1428 when the rulers of Tenochtitlan, Texcoco, and Tlacopan formed an alliance' (Acolhua page); Texcoco kept its tlatoani and received two-fifths of the tribute (Texcoco page).

capitals.name: Coatlinchan
capitals.note: 'Their first capital was Coatlinchan, later moving to the more famous Tetzcoco.' The coordinates are the town's, not from a page.

capitals.name: Tetzcoco (Texcoco)
capitals.note: 'In or about 1337, the Acolhua, with Tepanec help, expelled Chichimecs from Tetzcoco'; 'Tetzcoco became the Acolhua capital city, taking over that role from Coatlinchan.' Coordinates are the gazetteer's historic site.

rulers.name: Quinatzin
rulers.note: The page's list. Xolotl, 'said to be the founder of Tetzcoco in 1115 AD and reigned until 1232', is not in the list; 1232-1298 is not on the page.

rulers.name: Ixtlilxochitl I
rulers.note: 'In 1418, Ixtlilxochitl I, the tlatoani (ruler) of Tetzcoco, was dethroned by Tezozomoc of Azcapotzalco.'

rulers.name: Nezahualcoyotl
rulers.note: The page's list has 1420-1472; the dossier stops at 1428 with the state. He 'fled into exile' when Maxtla turned against the Acolhua (Tepanec War page) and allied with the Mexica in 1428.

correction.text: 'The Acolhua settled most of the eastern Basin of Mexico, an area known as Acolhuacan': a 30 km disc round Texcoco and Coatlinchan

keyframe_review.note: 1202-1325, 2,632 km2 against the disc's 2,800 km2 (equal within a factor of two). Cliopatria's 10 cells straddle the south of the lake (Xochimilco, Chalco, Coatlinchan) and miss Texcoco's cell for the 1326 shape. The Acolhua 'arrived in the Valley of Mexico in or around the year 1200'; the page names Coatlinchan as the first capital. The Texcoco article's 450 hectares is the city, not the domain. [Reviewer am-03, 2026-10-18: region now excludes the Mexico City cell (Tenochtitlan), which the 30 km Texcoco disc reached]

correction.text: 'The Acolhua settled most of the eastern Basin of Mexico, an area known as Acolhuacan' with Tetzcoco as capital after about 1337

keyframe_review.note: 1326-1421, 2,132 km2 (seven cells south of the lake, Xochimilco, Chalco and Coatlinchan side, none the Texcoco cell). Corrected to the same eastern-Basin disc as before. 'Tetzcoco became the Acolhua capital city, taking over that role from Coatlinchan' in or about 1337. The Aztec-era domain 'beyond to Tollantzinco and Cuauhchinanco' (Acolhua page) is later and belongs to the Triple Alliance. [Reviewer am-03, 2026-10-18: region now excludes the Mexico City cell (Tenochtitlan), which the 30 km Texcoco disc reached]

correction.text: The same eastern-Basin disc, under Tepanec domination until 1428: 'In 1418, Ixtlilxochitl I, the tlatoani (ruler) of Tetzcoco, was dethroned by Tezozomoc of Azcapotzalco'

keyframe_review.note: 1422-1428, the same 2,132 km2 shape as 1326-1421. The Tepanec overlord dethroned the ruler in 1418; Nezahualcoyotl rules from 1420 and was in exile when Maxtla turned against the Acolhua (Tepanec War page); the ledger marks the Tepanec hold as a contest. [Reviewer am-03, 2026-10-18: region now excludes the Mexico City cell (Tenochtitlan), which the 30 km Texcoco disc reached]

region.text: most of the eastern Basin of Mexico, Acolhuacan

ledger.note: c. 1200: the Acolhua settle the eastern Basin of Mexico. 'arrived in the Valley of Mexico in or around the year 1200'; 'Their first capital was Coatlinchan'. The Texcoco page has 'Tetzcoco was founded in the 12th century ... probably by the Chichimecs' and Xolotl as founder 'in 1115 AD'; 1202 is Cliopatria's year. [Reviewer am-03, 2026-10-18: region now excludes the Mexico City cell (Tenochtitlan), which the 30 km Texcoco disc reached]

region.text: Tetzcoco, from which Chichimecs were expelled

ledger.note: c. 1337: the Acolhua take Tetzcoco and make it their capital. 'In or about 1337, the Acolhua, with Tepanec help, expelled Chichimecs from Tetzcoco'; 'Tetzcoco became the Acolhua capital city, taking over that role from Coatlinchan.'
c. 1337: the Acolhua capital moves from Coatlinchan to Tetzcoco (identity.capitals).

region.text: Tetzcoco and the Acolhua kingdom under Tepanec rule

ledger.note: 1418: Tezozomoc of Azcapotzalco dethrones the ruler of Texcoco. 'In 1418, Ixtlilxochitl I, the tlatoani (ruler) of Tetzcoco, was dethroned by Tezozomoc of Azcapotzalco.' The page gives no campaign or boundary; the Tepanec hold on Texcoco lasts to the war of 1427-1428 (Maxtla turned on the Acolhua after Tezozomoc died in 1426 and Nezahualcoyotl 'fled into exile', Tepanec War page) and is drawn as one contest (confidence 2). [Reviewer am-03, 2026-10-18: region now excludes the Mexico City cell (Tenochtitlan), which the 30 km Texcoco disc reached]

1428: Nezahualcoyotl and the Mexica defeat Azcapotzalco. 'Ten years later, in 1428, Ixtlilxochitl's son, Nezahualcoyotl allied' with the Mexica 'to defeat Tezozomoc's son and successor, Maxtla' (Texcoco page); 'emerging victorious in 1428' (Tepanec War page). [Reviewer am-03, 2026-10-18: region now excludes the Mexico City cell (Tenochtitlan), which the 30 km Texcoco disc reached]

1428: Texcoco joins Tenochtitlan and Tlacopan in the Triple Alliance. 'founded in 1428 when the rulers of Tenochtitlan, Texcoco, and Tlacopan formed an alliance'. The Texcoco page gives it two-fifths of the tribute; no year for the formal treaty (1430 on the Tepanec War page). [Reviewer am-03, 2026-10-18: region was Cliopatria's misplaced Texcoco shape (south of the lake); now the corrected disc]

region.text: the independent kingdom, continued within the Triple Alliance

ledger.note: 1428: independent Texcoco ends as the second partner of the Aztec Triple Alliance (the tlatoani and the city continue to 1521). [Reviewer am-03, 2026-10-18: region was Cliopatria's misplaced Texcoco shape (south of the lake); now the corrected disc]

wars.name: Tepanec domination and the Tepanec War
wars.outcome: Ixtlilxochitl I was dethroned by Tezozomoc in 1418; Maxtla turned on the Acolhua in 1426 and Nezahualcoyotl fled; in 1427-1428 the allies defeated Azcapotzalco and formed the Triple Alliance.
wars.note: The Tepanec War page (the Aztec Empire article) dates the war 1427 to 1428 and the treaty 1430. The Texcoco page does not describe a 1426-1428 war or Nezahualcoyotl's return.

certainty.note: The pages give 'most of the eastern Basin of Mexico' only; no border is known.

sources.title: Texcoco (altepetl)
sources.note: Founding in the 12th century, c. 1337 capital, rulers' list, 1418 dethroning, 1428 alliance, two-fifths of the tribute, 450 hectares.

sources.title: Acolhua
sources.note: Arrival c. 1200, first capital Coatlinchan, Acolhuacan in the eastern Basin, alliance founded in 1428.

sources.title: Tepanec War (redirects to Aztec Empire)
sources.note: The request redirected to the Aztec Empire article: 1426 succession crisis, Nezahualcoyotl's exile, war 1427-1428, treaty 1430.

notes: Three pages (budget 1-2; the third is the Aztec Empire page opened for the Triple Alliance). (1) CLIOPATRIA SHAPES: the 1202 shape (ten cells, 99.16-98.73 W, 18.93-19.42 N) and the 1326-1428 shape (seven cells) lie south and south-east of the lake and neither contains the Texcoco cell for 1326-1428; Cliopatria's Tenochtitlan shape from 1326 sits over the Texcoco area. All three are corrected to the 30 km disc round Texcoco. The disc is my reading of 'most of the eastern Basin'. (2) START 1202 is Cliopatria's; the Acolhua page says 'in or around the year 1200'; the Texcoco page's 1115 for Xolotl is not used. (3) END 1428, with the alliance; Cliopatria also ends in 1428 and starts the Triple Alliance in 1429, the dossier of which starts in 1428. (4) CONTEST 1418-1428: the Tepanec hold is drawn as a contest between the Acolhua and Azcapotzalco; a vassal reading is also possible. (5) The Texcoco article does not name the 1426-1428 war nor Nezahualcoyotl's return; those come from the Tepanec War (Aztec Empire) page. (6) Rulers: the page's list, clipped at 1428; Xolotl is outside the list. (7) Coatlinchan has no gazetteer entry; the coordinates are the town's (19.44 N, 98.88 W).
